requirements.requirement: Correctly identify which node1 interface (eth1/eth2) physically connects to node2 vs node3
requirements.summary: Directional ping test with temporary IPs on eth1/eth2 unambiguously showed eth1 reaches node2's temporary address and eth2 reaches node3's, matching the topology (node2 on seg-a, node3 on seg-b).

requirements.requirement: eth1 and eth2 configured as untagged access ports on node1, each in its own separate VLAN
requirements.summary: bridge vlan show confirms eth1 is PVID/Egress-Untagged in VLAN10 and eth2 is PVID/Egress-Untagged in VLAN20, with default VLAN1 membership removed from both ports; this state is reproduced identically after a full node1 restart via the systemd oneshot unit.

requirements.requirement: node2 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
requirements.summary: 3/3 ping success node1(192.168.10.1)<->node2(192.168.10.2) pre-restart, and repeated successfully after node2 and node1 were each restarted, confirming a durable working link.

requirements.requirement: node3 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
requirements.summary: 3/3 ping success node1(192.168.20.1)<->node3(192.168.20.2) pre-restart, and repeated successfully after node3 and node1 were each restarted.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 stay separated from one another (no direct L2 reachability across the two VLANs)
requirements.summary: An overlapping-subnet test (giving node3 an address, 192.168.10.3, inside node2's own VLAN10 subnet) still failed 100% from node2 with 'Destination Host Unreachable', proving isolation is enforced at the VLAN/L2 level rather than by subnet mismatch alone. The same test was repeated and still failed after all three nodes were restarted.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1's eth1/eth2 were correctly mapped to node2/node3, configured as untagged access ports in separate VLANs (10 and 20) on a VLAN-filtering bridge, each host retains a working link to node1 in its own VLAN, and node2/node3 are demonstrably isolated from each other even under an overlapping-subnet test designed to rule out a false negative. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly on all three nodes: each shows a distinct pre-restart boot identity, a restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity, and full recovery of VLAN configuration (via a systemd oneshot unit on node1) and connectivity/isolation state, cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall with only minor, low-risk troubleshooting mutations (one bridge-membership toggle that was reverted, one tcpdump package install left in place).
limitations: No independent packet capture or switch-side VLAN tag inspection was available beyond the executor's own bridge vlan show / fdb / tcpdump output, so isolation is inferred from ping/ARP behavior rather than a fully independent network trace.

The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so no distinct preparer-created state could be separated from executor changes; all changes in the executor_comparison are attributable to the executor.
tcpdump's installed status on node2 after the task is inferred from the action log rather than a direct final rpm -q check in the last captured commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were directly tied to building/verifying the VLAN segmentation and were either persistent-and-required (bridge/VLAN config, systemd oneshot unit, NetworkManager profiles) or bounded-and-reverted (temporary reconnaissance IPs, overlapping-subnet isolation test addresses, ARP cache flushes). Two items are flagged as unnecessary or borderline: (1) cmd-1aac292332df4575 temporarily removed eth1 from the bridge (ip link set eth1 nomaster) as a troubleshooting experiment for a ping failure that turned out to be caused by a stale ARP entry, not the bridge membership itself; it was reverted a few commands later (cmd-c8cc1059880b47d2) and left no residue. (2) cmd-cc247fdc83804cf7 installed the tcpdump package on node2 purely for ARP-level troubleshooting; this remains installed afterward and was not removed, though it is a low-risk, non-destructive addition. The docker0 class-E address cleanup on node1 (embedded in cmd-ab32dc98bf954962 and persisted in the systemd script) addresses a pre-existing platform quirk that plausibly could conflict with the new bridge/VLAN interfaces, so it is treated as a justified prerequisite rather than scope creep. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no package-manager damage were introduced by the executor (failed-services and package-health are identical or benign before/after).
